newsitem.title: UK: New BA image both traditional, futuristic.
newsitem.headline: New BA image both traditional, futuristic.

text.p: British Airways Plc on Tuesday returned to the traditional red, white and blue of the Union Jack when it unveiled its new livery and corporate identity.
The company has given its new image an added flourish with plans to decorate the tail fins of its fleet of 300 aircraft with specially commissioned designs from artists from around the world.

The makeover, which will cost about 60 million pounds ($98.1 million) over three years, will be the first overhaul since BA swapped the national flag for its rather sombre livery of dark blue, red and grey in 1984, when the airline was being prepared for privatisation.
The new design cost BA about two million pounds but it will have to spend far more making the changes.
"For 14 years we have traded very successfully but there's always a time for change and I think that time is now," chief executive Bob Ayling said.
The airline had said it was not dropping the British Airways' brand but wanted to become more international in its image as it pressed ahead with its aim to become a global airline.

BA and American Airlines announced last year they intended to form an alliance to market each other's flights as their own but the so-called "open skies" pact is awaiting U.S., British and European Commission approval.
"Airlines are extraordinarily chauvinistic companies," Ayling said. "And I think with more deregulation in the world, they have to become more cosmopolitan."
Ayling said the company's image had seemed "staid and cold".
"We wanted an image more representative of the people we are...creative and friendly," he said.
